title: Audit Evidence (SA 500, 501, 505, 510, 530 & 550) – Sufficient Appropriate Evidence, Selected Items, External Confirmations, Opening Balances, Audit Sampling and Related Parties
description: CA Final – Auditing and Assurance | Advanced MCQ practice bank for the Audit Evidence chapter, built from the SA 500, 501, 505, 510, 530 and 550 study notes. Covers: the meaning of audit evidence as information used in arriving at the conclusions on which the opinion is based, including both financial and other information, and the hierarchy of risk assessment and further audit procedures (tests of controls directed at operating effectiveness in preventing, detecting and correcting misstatement, versus substantive procedures directed at detecting it), together with the seven methods of obtaining evidence (inquiry, observation, inspection, recalculation, re-performance, external confirmation and analytical procedures) and the three ways of selecting items for testing; the auditor's evaluation and use of the work of a management expert, including competence, capability and objectivity, the sources of information about them, the appropriateness of the expert's findings, assumptions, methods and source data, the five threats to the expert's objectivity and the seven factors governing the extent of the auditor's procedures. It covers the SA 501 selected items: physical inventory counting where inventory is material, attendance at the count, a count held at a date other than the date of the financial statement, unforeseen circumstances preventing attendance, impracticability of attendance, inventory held by third parties, litigation and claims and communication with external legal counsel, and segment information. It covers SA 505 external confirmations: positive, negative and blank confirmation requests, exceptions and non-responses, design factors, management's refusal to allow a confirmation request, the four conditions for relying on negative confirmations and the reliability of responses. It covers SA 510 opening balances in an initial audit engagement, SA 530 audit sampling including sampling risk, the two erroneous conclusions, sample size, the five methods of selection, stratification, treatment of items and evaluation of results, and SA 550 related parties including the definition and the state-control exception, inquiry of management, the engagement team discussion, alertness while inspecting records, previously unidentified or undisclosed related parties, significant transactions outside the normal course of business, disclosures, written representations and communication with those charged with governance. Every question is independently usable: where several questions draw on one case study, the complete case is repeated inside each of them.

questions.category: SA 500 – Purpose and Definition of Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Assertion (A): SA 500 explains what constitutes audit evidence in the audit of financial statements and deals with the auditor's responsibility to design and perform procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence.

Reason (R): Because an opinion on financial statements can be formed only from accounting data, audit evidence is confined to financial information used by the auditor.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
questions.explanation: The assertion reproduces the purpose of SA 500 as stated in the source, so it is correct. The reason fails at its premise: audit evidence means information used by the auditor in arriving at the conclusions on which the opinion is based, and it includes both financial information and other information. Non-financial information is therefore within the scope of evidence, and the source itself illustrates this by defining analytical procedures as a study of plausible relationships among both financial and non-financial data. Since R is incorrect, the last two options fall away, and a true assertion cannot be explained by a false proposition.

questions.category: SA 500 – Purpose and Definition of Audit Evidence
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the scope of audit evidence is NOT correct?
options: Audit evidence includes both financial information and other information used by the auditor in arriving at the conclusions on which the auditor's opinion is based.
Information used by the auditor in arriving at the conclusions on which the opinion is based constitutes audit evidence, even where that information is non-financial in character.
SA 500 explains what constitutes audit evidence and deals with the auditor's responsibility to design and perform procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence.
The auditor's responsibility under SA 500 is discharged by obtaining audit evidence; the design of the procedures is a matter of the partner's judgment and is outside the scope of this SA.
questions.explanation: The purpose sentence in the source is explicit that the SA deals with the auditor's responsibility to design AND perform procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, so severing design from the SA's scope is the incorrect statement. Options 1 and 2 are simply the two halves of the definition, which expressly includes both financial and other information. Option 3 restates the purpose faithfully. The decisive point is that design is not left outside the standard; a candidate who reads the responsibility as merely one of collection has missed half of the sentence.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the framework of audit procedures, risk assessment procedures are directed at identifying the risk of material misstatement, whereas tests of controls are directed at evaluating the operating effectiveness of controls.

Reason (R): Tests of controls and substantive procedures are both classified as further audit procedures.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both propositions are supported by the source table: risk assessment procedures are the audit procedures to identify the risk of material misstatement as given in SA 315, and tests of controls evaluate operating effectiveness. R is also a correct statement of the table structure, since the further audit procedures heading contains tests of controls and substantive procedures. However R does not explain A; the difference in purpose between the two kinds of procedure flows from their separate definitions, not from the fact that both fall on one side or the other of a dividing line. Classification tells you where a procedure sits, not what it is designed to do.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the classification of audit procedures under SA 500:

**Statement 1:** Risk assessment procedures are the audit procedures performed to identify the risk of material misstatement, and the source of that requirement is SA 315.
**Statement 2:** Substantive procedures comprise tests of details of classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures as well as substantive analytical procedures.
**Statement 3:** Tests of controls form part of risk assessment procedures because they evaluate how well controls prevent, detect and correct material misstatements.
**Statement 4:** Analytical procedures constitute a separate category of audit procedure standing outside both risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 reproduce the table correctly: risk assessment procedures identify the risk of material misstatement under SA 315, and substantive procedures comprise tests of details of classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures plus substantive analytical procedures. Statement 3 is wrong because tests of controls sit under further audit procedures, not under risk assessment procedures; the wording of a test of controls is what makes it sound risk-identifying, and that is the trap. Statement 4 is wrong because analytical procedures appear in the table of methods used to obtain evidence in performing the above procedures, so they cut across the classification rather than standing outside it.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Evaluating whether a control operates effectively is complete once the auditor confirms that the control prevents material misstatements, since detection and correction are the concerns of substantive procedures.

Reason (R): A test of controls is an audit procedure designed to evaluate the operating effectiveness of controls in preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The definition in the source lists three functions conjunctively: preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements. The assertion truncates that list to prevention alone and then mislabels the omitted two as the province of substantive procedures, which is precisely the confusion this question tests. The reason restates the definition accurately and is therefore correct on its own terms. Because the reason is the very wording that defeats the assertion, the fourth option is the only sustainable answer; substantive procedures are designed to detect material misstatements, not to evaluate operating effectiveness of controls.

questions.question: While designing the extent of testing over a class of transactions, an auditor must choose an approach to selecting items for testing. Which one of the following is NOT one of the approaches identified in SA 500 for selecting items for testing?
options: Selecting all items, that is, 100% examination
questions.explanation: The source presents selecting items for testing as a three-cell taxonomy only: selecting all items or 100% examination, selecting specific items, and audit sampling. Substantive analytical procedures belong to a different row of the same framework, being one of the two components of substantive procedures, so it is the odd one out. The question works because both rows are taught on the same page and candidates routinely cross-file them. The other three options are exactly the three permitted approaches in the words used by the source.

questions.question:
Match Column I with Column II.

Column I
A: Risk assessment procedures
B: Tests of controls
C: Substantive procedures
D: Analytical procedures

Column II
1: Audit procedure designed to detect material misstatements
2: Audit procedure to identify the risk of material misstatement
3: Evaluations of financial information by study of plausible relationships among both financial and non-financial data
4: Audit procedure designed to evaluate operating effectiveness of controls in preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Risk assessment procedures match 2 because the table defines them as the procedures to identify the risk of material misstatement. Tests of controls match 4 and substantive procedures match 1; these two are the pair candidates reverse, since both are concerned with material misstatements and the difference lies in whether operating effectiveness or the misstatement itself is being addressed. Analytical procedures match 3, a method-level definition deliberately placed here to test whether the candidate notices that a method and a procedural classification operate at different levels of the same page.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question: When information that is to be used as audit evidence has been prepared using the work of a management's expert, SA 500 sets out three mandatory steps. Which one of the following represents the correct sequence in which those three steps are listed in the source?
options: Evaluate competence, capability and objectivity; evaluate appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence; obtain an understanding of the work of that expert.
Evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence; evaluate competence, capability and objectivity; obtain an understanding of the work of that expert.
Evaluate competence, capability and objectivity; obtain an understanding of the work of that expert; evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence.
Obtain an understanding of the work of that expert; evaluate competence, capability and objectivity; evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence.
questions.explanation: The source enumerates the three shall requirements as (i) evaluate the competence, capability and objectivity of that expert, (ii) obtain an understanding of the work of that expert, and (iii) evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence. Option 3 is that order. The three distractors each preserve all three activities but invert the last two or lead with the evaluation of appropriateness, which would have the auditor judging the output of work it has not yet understood. All three are mandatory whenever evidence is prepared using the work of a management's expert, so no option that omits or subordinates one of them can be right.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question: Which one of the following descriptions of a method of obtaining audit evidence is NOT correct?
options: Inquiry consists of seeking information of knowledgeable persons, both financial and non-financial, whether those persons are within or outside the entity.
Observation consists of looking at a process being performed by others.
Re-performance consists of checking the arithmetical accuracy of documents or records.
Inspection involves examining records or documents, whether internal or external, in paper form, electronic form or other media, or the physical examination of an asset.
questions.explanation: Checking arithmetical accuracy of documents or records is the definition of recalculation, not of re-performance. Re-performance is the auditor's independent execution of procedures or controls, a qualitatively different act because the auditor performs rather than merely verifies addition. The other three descriptions are faithful to the source, including the points that inquiry reaches persons outside the entity and that inspection covers electronic and other media as well as physical examination of an asset. These two methods are the most frequently interchanged pair in the seven-method table.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question: Which one of the following best reflects the source's description of external confirmation as a method of obtaining audit evidence?
options: It is a written response obtained by the auditor from a third party, and the detailed requirements governing confirmation requests, positive and negative confirmations and exceptions are dealt with separately.
It is a form of audit evidence obtained by the auditor as a direct written response to the auditor from a third party, that third party being the confirming party.
It is a procedure in which the auditor independently executes the confirmation control operated by the entity and compares the result with the entity's records.
It is an inquiry addressed to an external knowledgeable person whose written reply supplies the corroborative audit evidence for the assertion.
It is an inspection of documents originating outside the entity which the auditor obtains from the client's files.
questions.explanation: The single line devoted to external confirmation in the methods table defines it as audit evidence obtained by the auditor as a direct written response to the auditor from a third party, the confirming party. The decisive words are direct and response, because they distinguish confirmation from inspection of externally-originated documents held in the client's files, which is option 5. Option 4 dresses up inquiry in confirmation clothing and option 3 describes re-performance. Option 1 is unsupportable at the level of this source, which makes no reference to confirmation request mechanics or to exceptions, so it cannot be the best reflection of the line.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Match the activities in Column I with the methods of obtaining audit evidence in Column II.

Column I
A: The auditor evaluates the adequacy of the provision for warranty claims by studying the relationship between the entity's claim rate per thousand units shipped and the movement in service-cost spend over three years.
B: The auditor checks the arithmetical accuracy of the depreciation schedule prepared by the entity by re-adding the columns and agreeing the total to the ledger.
C: The auditor asks the Fund Manager of an externally managed scheme to explain the treatment adopted for a securities transaction, being a person with the relevant knowledge.
D: The auditor independently executes the period-end cut-off control that the entity operates over its shipping documents.

Column II
1: Recalculation
2: Re-performance
3: Analytical procedures
4: Inquiry

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Activity A evaluates financial information by studying plausible relationships among financial and non-financial data, namely claim rates against units shipped, which is analytical procedures. Activity B is arithmetical checking and is recalculation, not re-performance, because nothing is independently executed beyond verification of addition. Activity C seeks information of a knowledgeable person and is inquiry notwithstanding that the person is outside the entity, since inquiry expressly reaches outside. Activity D is the auditor's independent execution of a control and is therefore re-performance, the classic confusion being to call it observation.

questions.question:
Consider the following four situations:

Situation 1: A salaried officer in the entity's own internal valuation cell prepares the actuarial-style computation supporting the measurement of a biological asset.
Situation 2: A firm of valuers whose work on mine closure obligations is used by the entity to assist it in preparing its financial statements.
Situation 3: A firm engaged directly by the Board's Audit Committee, entirely outside India, whose valuation is reflected in the entity's financial statements.
Situation 4: The entity's Chief Financial Officer, a fellow chartered accountant, prepares the fair value disclosure for a financial instrument.

Which of these involve a management's expert as defined in SA 500?
questions.explanation: A management's expert is an individual or organisation possessing expertise in a field other than accounting or auditing, whose work in that field is used by the entity to assist the entity in preparing the financial statements; the entity may employ or engage such experts. Situations 1, 2 and 3 each satisfy that definition, and the examples given in the source are actuarial calculations and valuations. Situation 4 fails because the CFO's expertise is in accounting, which the definition expressly excludes. The trap is to exclude Situation 1 on the mistaken view that an expert must be external, which is why the combination including 1, 2 and 3 is right.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Consider the following statements made while an auditor evaluates whether an engineer's report on the residual value of plant may be used as audit evidence:

**Statement 1:** The report was prepared by an expert engaged by the entity to assist it in preparing financial statements, so the expert is not a management's expert because the definition admits only experts employed by the entity.
**Statement 2:** The auditor may obtain information about the expert's competence, capability and objectivity from personal experience with the previous work of that expert, from discussion with that expert, from knowledge of the expert's qualifications and from published papers or books written by that expert.
**Statement 3:** Where the expert's work involves the use of significant assumptions and methods, the auditor considers the relevance and reasonableness of those assumptions and methods.
**Statement 4:** Where the expert's work involves the use of source data, the auditor considers the relevance and completeness of that source data.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is wrong because the source expressly says the entity may employ OR engage experts in other fields, so an engaged expert is squarely within the definition. Statement 2 lists the four sources of information about competence, capability and objectivity exactly as the source gives them: personal experience with previous work, discussion with the expert, knowledge of qualifications and published papers or books. Statements 3 and 4 are the second and third considerations on evaluating the appropriateness of the expert's work, and the wording matters because assumptions and methods attract a relevance and reasonableness test while source data attracts relevance and completeness.

questions.category: SA 500 – Threats to Objectivity of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about threats to the objectivity of a management's expert:

**Statement 1:** Circumstances that may threaten the expert's objectivity include self-interest, advocacy, familiarity, self-review and intimidation threats.
**Statement 2:** Safeguards may reduce such threats, but they cannot eliminate all threats to the expert's objectivity.
**Statement 3:** Because safeguards cannot eliminate all threats, the auditor obtains information about interests and relationships creating threats from management alone, since the expert is not the auditor's client.
**Statement 4:** The auditor shall discuss with both management and that expert any interests and relationships that may create threats to the expert's objectivity and any applicable safeguards.

Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is the only incorrect one. It accepts the true proposition that safeguards cannot eliminate all threats but draws the wrong consequence, narrowing the required discussion to management alone, whereas the source requires the auditor to discuss with management AND that expert. Statements 1, 2 and 4 restate the source: the five named threats, the reduce-but-cannot-eliminate limit on safeguards, and the two-sided discussion requirement. The question is framed so that a candidate who remembers the five threats but not the identity of the parties to be consulted will read statement 3 as a permissible interpretation.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Case study: In the audit of Meridian Pharma Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement partner, CA Rajesh Patel, documents five activities performed by his team:
A1: The audit senior sits in the despatch bay at the Manesar plant and watches the entity's independent stock verifier carrying out the routine quarterly count of finished formulations, without taking any part in the count.
A2: The audit junior takes the entity's bank reconciliation for March 2026 and independently executes the same matching and reconciling steps on the entity's data, arriving at the balance without reference to the result the entity had reached.
A3: The partner holds a structured discussion with the Chief Chemist, a person with the relevant knowledge, about how the batch-release control is operated, and records the answers in the file.
A4: The team checks the arithmetical accuracy of the schedule of job-work charges by re-adding the columns and re-extending the rate quantities.
A5: The team retrieves the Board minutes and the quality council minutes from the entity's electronic document repository and reads the extracts relevant to batch recalls.

With reference to the activities described above and to the methods of obtaining audit evidence in SA 500, match Column I with Column II.

Column I
A: Activity A1
B: Activity A2
C: Activity A3
D: Activity A4

Column II
1: Observation
2: Re-performance
3: Inquiry
4: Recalculation
5: Inspection

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: A1 is observation because the auditor looks at a process being performed by others and takes no part in it. A2 is re-performance, not observation and not recalculation, because the auditor independently executes the reconciling steps; the decisive fact is that the entity's own performance is not being watched at all. A3 is inquiry since it seeks information of a knowledgeable person, whether or not that person's knowledge is financial. A4 is recalculation because the work is checking arithmetical accuracy of a record, which differs from independently executing a control.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Case study: In the audit of Meridian Pharma Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement partner, CA Rajesh Patel, documents five activities performed by his team:
A1: The audit senior sits in the despatch bay at the Manesar plant and watches the entity's independent stock verifier carrying out the routine quarterly count of finished formulations, without taking any part in the count.
A2: The audit junior takes the entity's bank reconciliation for March 2026 and independently executes the same matching and reconciling steps on the entity's data, arriving at the balance without reference to the result the entity had reached.
A3: The partner holds a structured discussion with the Chief Chemist, a person with the relevant knowledge, about how the batch-release control is operated, and records the answers in the file.
A4: The team checks the arithmetical accuracy of the schedule of job-work charges by re-adding the columns and re-extending the rate quantities.
A5: The team retrieves the Board minutes and the quality council minutes from the entity's electronic document repository and reads the extracts relevant to batch recalls.

Consider the following statements regarding activity A5:

**Statement 1:** A5 is inspection because it involves examining records or documents, and it is immaterial that those records were held in electronic form.
**Statement 2:** A5 cannot be inspection because inspection is confined to internal or external records examined in paper form.
**Statement 3:** A5 is inquiry because the auditor is seeking information from the minutes, which were prepared by knowledgeable persons.
**Statement 4:** Inspection also extends to physical examination of an asset, so A5 and a physical count of inventory both fall within the same method.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: inspection covers records or documents whether internal or external and in paper form, electronic form or other media, so the repository format does not defeat the classification. Statement 4 is also correct and identifies the second limb of the same definition, physical examination of an asset, which is why a document review and a count are both inspection. Statement 2 contradicts the express words of the definition. Statement 3 is the tempting error: reading a document is not seeking information of a knowledgeable person, so the method is inspection and not inquiry.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Case study: In the audit of Meridian Pharma Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement partner, CA Rajesh Patel, documents five activities performed by his team:
A1: The audit senior sits in the despatch bay at the Manesar plant and watches the entity's independent stock verifier carrying out the routine quarterly count of finished formulations, without taking any part in the count.
A2: The audit junior takes the entity's bank reconciliation for March 2026 and independently executes the same matching and reconciling steps on the entity's data, arriving at the balance without reference to the result the entity had reached.
A3: The partner holds a structured discussion with the Chief Chemist, a person with the relevant knowledge, about how the batch-release control is operated, and records the answers in the file.
A4: The team checks the arithmetical accuracy of the schedule of job-work charges by re-adding the columns and re-extending the rate quantities.
A5: The team retrieves the Board minutes and the quality council minutes from the entity's electronic document repository and reads the extracts relevant to batch recalls.

Consider the following statements regarding activity A3:

**Statement 1:** A3 is inquiry, since it consists of seeking information of a knowledgeable person, and inquiry may range from a formal written inquiry to an informal oral inquiry.
**Statement 2:** A3 is a test of controls because the auditor discussed how the batch-release control operates, and inquiry about the operation of a control is by itself a procedure to evaluate the operating effectiveness of that control.
**Statement 3:** A3 would still qualify as inquiry even if the Chief Chemist were a person engaged by the entity from outside it, because inquiry reaches knowledgeable persons both within and outside the entity.
**Statement 4:** Responses to an inquiry such as A3 may provide corroborative audit evidence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is the incorrect one. Evaluating the operating effectiveness of controls in preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements is the definition of a test of controls, and a discussion with the Chemist remains, at the level of method, an inquiry; treating that inquiry as itself evaluating operating effectiveness is the classification error the statement invites. Statement 1 is correct as to the definition and as to the range of inquiry from formal written to informal oral. Statement 3 is correct because the definition extends to persons within or outside the entity, and statement 4 is correct because responses to inquiries may provide corroborative audit evidence.

questions.category: SA 500 – Methods of Obtaining Audit Evidence
questions.question:
Case study: In the audit of Meridian Pharma Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement partner, CA Rajesh Patel, documents five activities performed by his team:
A1: The audit senior sits in the despatch bay at the Manesar plant and watches the entity's independent stock verifier carrying out the routine quarterly count of finished formulations, without taking any part in the count.
A2: The audit junior takes the entity's bank reconciliation for March 2026 and independently executes the same matching and reconciling steps on the entity's data, arriving at the balance without reference to the result the entity had reached.
A3: The partner holds a structured discussion with the Chief Chemist, a person with the relevant knowledge, about how the batch-release control is operated, and records the answers in the file.
A4: The team checks the arithmetical accuracy of the schedule of job-work charges by re-adding the columns and re-extending the rate quantities.
A5: The team retrieves the Board minutes and the quality council minutes from the entity's electronic document repository and reads the extracts relevant to batch recalls.

Which one of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE classification of activity A2?
options: Observation, because the auditor is watching a reconciliation that the entity's accounts staff have already completed.
Recalculation, because the auditor is re-working figures and checking their arithmetical accuracy.
Inspection, because the auditor is examining a record, namely the bank reconciliation statement.
Analytical procedures, because the auditor evaluates the relationship between the bank balance and the ledger balance.
Re-performance, because the auditor independently executes a procedure or control rather than watching others perform it or merely checking addition.
questions.explanation: Re-performance is the auditor's independent execution of procedures or controls, and A2 says in terms that the junior performs the matching and reconciling steps without reference to the entity's result. Observation fails because no process is being performed by others in the auditor's presence; the entity's staff are absent from the scene described. Recalculation fails because the auditor is executing a reconciling process, not checking arithmetical accuracy of a document. Inspection fails because the record is an input to a re-performed procedure rather than evidence examined in itself.

questions.question:
Case study: During the audit of Vardhman Cables Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement team led by CA Ila Swaminathan notices that a contract with the entity's largest customer contains an unusual price-rebate mechanism for which no supporting computation exists in the accounting records. The Chief Financial Officer explains orally that the rebate is administered entirely by the sales team and has never been audited before. The auditor considers obtaining a written representation from the CFO confirming that oral response. She also puts a formal written question to the customer's finance manager, a person knowledgeable about the commercial terms, seeking details of the mechanism.

Consider the following statements:

**Statement 1:** The auditor may obtain a written representation to confirm the response given to the oral inquiry made to the Chief Financial Officer.
**Statement 2:** The formal written question to the customer's finance manager is still within inquiry, because inquiries may range from formal written inquiries to informal oral inquiries and may be addressed to knowledgeable persons outside the entity.
**Statement 3:** The response obtained from the Chief Financial Officer may provide corroborative audit evidence.
**Statement 4:** Information sought under inquiry must relate to financial matters, so the commercial explanation given by the CFO falls outside inquiry.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 all track the inquiry row of the methods table, which permits a range from formal written to informal oral inquiry, extends to knowledgeable persons within or outside the entity, contemplates a written representation confirming responses to oral inquiries, and treats inquiry responses as capable of providing corroborative audit evidence. Statement 4 is the error: inquiry covers knowledgeable persons both financial and non-financial, so a commercial explanation is squarely within it. A candidate who treats non-financial answers as outside the method will also wrongly reject statement 2.

questions.question:
Case study: During the audit of Vardhman Cables Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement team led by CA Ila Swaminathan notices that a contract with the entity's largest customer contains an unusual price-rebate mechanism for which no supporting computation exists in the accounting records. The Chief Financial Officer explains orally that the rebate is administered entirely by the sales team and has never been audited before. The auditor considers obtaining a written representation from the CFO confirming that oral response. She also puts a formal written question to the customer's finance manager, a person knowledgeable about the commercial terms, seeking details of the mechanism.

Assertion (A): The auditor is entitled to address inquiry to the customer's finance manager and to treat the reply as audit evidence used in arriving at her conclusions.

Reason (R): Inquiry consists of seeking information of knowledgeable persons, both financial and non-financial, within or outside the entity.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion is correct because the definition of inquiry extends to knowledgeable persons outside the entity, and the reply is information used by the auditor in arriving at her conclusions and therefore audit evidence. The reason is a correct statement of the definition, and it is precisely the words within or outside the entity that license the auditor's course of action, so R explains A. Had the reason instead recited some other feature of inquiry, such as its range from formal to informal, it would have been correct without explaining the assertion, which is the distinction this item forces the candidate to draw.

questions.question:
Case study: Aurora Crop Sciences Limited measures a large mango plantation carried as a biological asset using a yield-projection model. The model is prepared by Dr. Neelima Sen, a horticultural statistician who is a whole-time employee of the entity's internal Agri-Insights Cell, that is, she is employed by the entity rather than engaged by it. CA Deepak Bhandari is the engagement partner for FY 2025-26. He records that Dr. Sen has written a published paper on non-linear yield extrapolation, that he has personal experience of her work in the two earlier audits, and that she holds a doctorate in horticultural statistics. He further notes that Dr. Sen's fee is partly linked to the surplus reported on the plantation and that she is the younger sister of the Whole-time Director who signs the financial statements.

Consider the following statements about how the framework in SA 500 applies to Dr. Sen:

**Statement 1:** Because Dr. Sen is employed by the entity and is not an external party, her work cannot be that of a management's expert, and the auditor need not evaluate her competence, capability and objectivity.
**Statement 2:** Whether the management's expert is employed by the entity or engaged by it is one of the factors the auditor considers in this area.
**Statement 3:** The auditor shall discuss with management and with Dr. Sen any interests and relationships that may create threats to her objectivity and any applicable safeguards.
**Statement 4:** The auditor may obtain information about Dr. Sen's competence, capability and objectivity from his personal experience with her previous work, from discussion with her, from knowledge of her qualifications and from her published paper.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is wrong on two counts. The definition of a management's expert expressly contemplates that the entity may employ or engage experts in other fields, so an internal expert is within it; and where evidence is prepared using that work the three shall requirements apply whatever the contractual form. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: employed versus engaged is one of the listed factors, the discussion of interests, relationships and safeguards must be with management and that expert, and the four sources of competence information include personal experience, discussion, qualifications and published work.

questions.category: SA 500 – Threats to Objectivity of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: Aurora Crop Sciences Limited measures a large mango plantation carried as a biological asset using a yield-projection model. The model is prepared by Dr. Neelima Sen, a horticultural statistician who is a whole-time employee of the entity's internal Agri-Insights Cell, that is, she is employed by the entity rather than engaged by it. CA Deepak Bhandari is the engagement partner for FY 2025-26. He records that Dr. Sen has written a published paper on non-linear yield extrapolation, that he has personal experience of her work in the two earlier audits, and that she holds a doctorate in horticultural statistics. He further notes that Dr. Sen's fee is partly linked to the surplus reported on the plantation and that she is the younger sister of the Whole-time Director who signs the financial statements.

The two facts about Dr. Sen's variable fee and her family relationship with the Whole-time Director are analysed by the engagement team. Which one of the following statements regarding those threats is NOT correct?
options: A fee linked to the reported surplus is capable of creating a self-interest threat to the expert's objectivity.
A close family relationship with the director who signs the financial statements is capable of creating a familiarity threat to the expert's objectivity.
Safeguards applied to Dr. Sen's position can reduce the threats and, if sufficiently strong, can eliminate all of them.
The auditor shall discuss with both management and Dr. Sen the interests and relationships that may create threats to her objectivity and any applicable safeguards.
questions.explanation: The source is categorical that safeguards may reduce such threats but cannot eliminate all threats, so option 3 overstates what safeguards can achieve and is the incorrect statement. Options 1 and 2 illustrate two of the five named threats, self-interest and familiarity, applied to these facts. Option 4 states the discussion obligation correctly, including that it runs to both management and the expert. The decisive word in option 3 is eliminate; a candidate who reads it as merely a stronger form of reduce has accepted the very proposition the source rules out.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: Aurora Crop Sciences Limited measures a large mango plantation carried as a biological asset using a yield-projection model. The model is prepared by Dr. Neelima Sen, a horticultural statistician who is a whole-time employee of the entity's internal Agri-Insights Cell, that is, she is employed by the entity rather than engaged by it. CA Deepak Bhandari is the engagement partner for FY 2025-26. He records that Dr. Sen has written a published paper on non-linear yield extrapolation, that he has personal experience of her work in the two earlier audits, and that she holds a doctorate in horticultural statistics. He further notes that Dr. Sen's fee is partly linked to the surplus reported on the plantation and that she is the younger sister of the Whole-time Director who signs the financial statements.

Now assume that, instead of being a whole-time employee of the Agri-Insights Cell, Dr. Sen is a partner of an independent consultancy engaged by the entity on a per-report basis, everything else in the case remaining unchanged. Which one of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE consequence of that single change?
options: Dr. Sen ceases to be a management's expert, so the three mandatory evaluations fall away.
The change is relevant because one of the listed factors is whether the management's expert is employed by the entity or engaged by it, and that factor now points the other way.
The change disposes of the need to discuss interests and relationships creating threats, because an external expert has no relationship with management.
The change makes it unnecessary to evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work, because an engaged expert is subject to market discipline.
The change alters the order in which the three mandatory steps must be performed.
questions.explanation: The definition admits experts whom the entity employs or engages, so neither the first nor the fourth option follows; the three mandatory requirements remain in force and in the same listed order whatever the contractual form. The source lists among the factors the question whether the management's expert is employed by the entity or engaged by it, so switching Dr. Sen from employed to engaged changes exactly one input to the auditor's analysis. Option 3 is wrong because a per-report engagement can still involve interests and relationships, and the discussion duty with management and the expert is unconditional.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: Chandaria Bhushan Jain & Co. audit Suraksha Port Holdings Limited for FY 2025-26. The residual value and removal-cost estimate for a large port crane have been determined using an actuarial-style computation prepared by Rangaswamy Survey & Engineering Associates, a firm engaged by the entity for that purpose. Engagement partner CA Anita Desai must address the requirements that apply where information to be used as audit evidence is prepared using the work of a management's expert. She has available the following possible actions:
1: Evaluate the competence, capability and objectivity of the firm.
2: Obtain an understanding of the work of the firm.
3: Evaluate the appropriateness of the firm's work as audit evidence.
4: Rely on the fact that safeguards adopted by the firm eliminate all threats to its objectivity, and on that basis omit the discussion of interests and relationships.
5: Dispense with obtaining an understanding of the firm's work because she has audited the output of this firm for four consecutive years.

Which one of the following sets of actions is the auditor required or permitted to take under SA 500?
questions.explanation: Actions 1, 2 and 3 are the three shall requirements and are mandatory whenever evidence is prepared using the work of a management's expert. Action 4 is defeated by the source's statement that safeguards may reduce such threats but cannot eliminate all of them, and the discussion of interests, relationships and safeguards must be held with both management and the expert. Action 5 fails because the obligation to obtain an understanding of the expert's work is not relieved by prior exposure to that work; previous experience of the expert's work bears on the extent of the auditor's procedures, not on whether a required step may be skipped.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: Chandaria Bhushan Jain & Co. audit Suraksha Port Holdings Limited for FY 2025-26. The residual value and removal-cost estimate for a large port crane have been determined using an actuarial-style computation prepared by Rangaswamy Survey & Engineering Associates, a firm engaged by the entity for that purpose. Engagement partner CA Anita Desai must address the requirements that apply where information to be used as audit evidence is prepared using the work of a management's expert.

Which one of the following is NOT a source from which the auditor may obtain information regarding the competence, capability and objectivity of that expert?
options: Personal experience with the previous work of that expert.
Knowledge of the qualifications of that expert.
The expert's own written representation confirming that it holds the professional qualifications current in that field.
Published papers or books written by that expert.
questions.explanation: The source gives four sources: personal experience with previous work of that expert, discussion with that expert, knowledge of the expert's qualifications, and published papers or books written by that expert. Option 4 is not among them; it converts the third source into a self-certifying representation by the expert, which is a different mechanism and is not what the source lists. The wording is deliberately close to knowledge of qualifications so that a candidate scanning for that phrase will accept it. Options 1, 2, 3 and 5 are the remaining listed sources.

questions.category: SA 500 – Using the Work of Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: Chandaria Bhushan Jain & Co. audit Suraksha Port Holdings Limited for FY 2025-26. The residual value and removal-cost estimate for a large port crane have been determined using an actuarial-style computation prepared by Rangaswamy Survey & Engineering Associates, a firm engaged by the entity for that purpose. Engagement partner CA Anita Desai must address the requirements that apply where information to be used as audit evidence is prepared using the work of a management's expert.

Match the activities in Column I with the requirements or considerations in Column II.

Column I
A: CA Desai obtains the firm's methodology note and reads how the removal-cost model is built.
B: CA Desai reads the firm's charter and its membership of a professional body, and recollects her experience of the firm in an earlier audit.
C: CA Desai re-computes the model output for one crane and agrees the source measurements used to the port trust's survey records.
D: CA Desai asks the entity and the firm whether the firm's fee arrangement with the entity creates any interest or relationship affecting the firm's objectivity, and what safeguards apply.

Column II
1: Obtain an understanding of the work of that expert.
2: Evaluate the competence, capability and objectivity of that expert.
3: Evaluate the appropriateness of the expert's work as audit evidence, including, where source data is used, the relevance and completeness of that source data.
4: Discuss with management and with the expert any interests and relationships that may create threats to the expert's objectivity and any applicable safeguards.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Reading how the model is built is obtaining an understanding of the work of the expert, not evaluating competence, which is the pairing candidates most often reverse. Qualifications, professional membership and the auditor's own previous experience are competence and objectivity inputs, so B matches 2. Re-computing output and agreeing source measurements addresses the appropriateness of the work as evidence and the relevance and completeness of source data. D is the objectivity discussion, a separate requirement which must be held with both management and the expert rather than being part of the appropriateness evaluation.

questions.category: SA 500 – Extent of Procedures on Management's Expert
questions.question:
Match the situations in Column I with the provisions in Column II.

Column I
A: The auditor notes that the matter on which an expert's report bears is a routine revaluation of a single listed debt instrument and that the risk of material misstatement in it is low.
B: The auditor finds that no other source of information exists for the measurement of a biological asset, so the expert's output is the only material available.
C: The entity's valuer is a salaried officer of its internal valuation cell rather than a firm engaged from outside.
D: The expert is bound by technical performance standards issued by a professional body, and the auditor has considerable experience of that field and of this expert's earlier reports.

Column II
1: Factors to be considered include the nature and complexity of the matter and the risk of material misstatement in the matter.
2: A factor to be considered is the availability of alternative sources of audit evidence.
3: A factor to be considered is whether the management's expert is employed by the entity or engaged by it.
4: Factors to be considered include whether the expert is subject to technical performance standards, the auditor's knowledge and experience of the expert's field of expertise, and the auditor's previous experience of the work of that expert.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Situation A engages the first two factors, the nature and complexity of the matter and the risk of material misstatement in it. Situation B is the availability of alternative sources of audit evidence, and situation C is the employed-or-engaged factor. Situation D bundles three factors that the source lists consecutively, namely subjection to technical performance standards, the auditor's knowledge and experience of the field, and the auditor's previous experience of that expert's work. The distractors split these by assigning the internal valuer to the technical standards factor, which is the pairing a hurried candidate would select.

questions.category: SA 500 – Evaluating the Expert's Work as Evidence
questions.question:
Case study: In auditing the fair value of an investment property, CA Nair's team takes four steps and records four conclusions.
Step 1: The auditor re-adds the columns of the expert's valuation sheet, finds one discounting cell arithmetically wrong, and concludes that arithmetical accuracy of the expert's findings is the relevance and completeness test required for source data.
Step 2: The auditor examines the expert's rent-growth and capitalisation-rate assumptions for relevance and reasonableness.
Step 3: The auditor establishes that the tenant schedule fed into the expert's model is complete by agreeing the count of leases to the lease register.
Step 4: The auditor compares the expert's valuation conclusion with pricing obtained for an adjacent property and finds them consistent.

Which one of the following correctly identifies the conclusion that misapplies the source's requirements for evaluating the expert's work?
options: Step 2, because assumptions and methods are considered only where the expert is engaged by the entity and not where employed.
Step 3, because completeness of source data is never a consideration in evaluating the expert's work.
Step 4, because consistency with other audit evidence falls outside the considerations for evaluating the appropriateness of the expert's work.
None of the conclusions misapplies the requirements.

Step 1, because arithmetical accuracy belongs to the method of recalculation, whereas the evaluation of the expert's work addresses relevance and reasonableness of findings or conclusions and their consistency with other audit evidence, and where source data is used, its relevance and completeness.
questions.explanation: Step 1 conflates two different things. Checking arithmetical accuracy of documents or records is the method of recalculation, while the requirement for evaluating the expert's work speaks of relevance and reasonableness of findings or conclusions and their consistency with other audit evidence, and of relevance and completeness where source data is used; attaching the source-data test to an arithmetic check misstates the framework. Steps 2, 3 and 4 each apply the correct limb: significant assumptions and methods attract relevance and reasonableness, source data attracts relevance and completeness, and findings are tested for consistency with other audit evidence. Options 1 and 2 invent distinctions the source does not draw.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding audit procedures:

**Statement 1:** A substantive procedure is an audit procedure designed to detect material misstatements.
**Statement 2:** Tests of details relate only to account balances, since classes of transactions and disclosures are addressed exclusively by substantive analytical procedures.
**Statement 3:** Tests of details and substantive analytical procedures are both components of substantive procedures.
**Statement 4:** Evaluating the operating effectiveness of controls in preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements is the purpose of tests of controls and not of substantive procedures.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is the definition of substantive procedures and statement 3 correctly identifies the two components, tests of details and substantive analytical procedures. Statement 2 is wrong because tests of details extend to classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures, so the restriction to balances is a narrowing error. Statement 4 marks the boundary with the row above: evaluating operating effectiveness is the definition of a test of controls, while detection of the misstatement itself is the purpose of substantive work.

questions.category: SA 500 – Integrated: Procedures, Methods and Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: In planning the audit of Kavach Sentinel Systems Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement team performs five activities:
A1: The team studies the relationship between units shipped, the size of the installed base and warranty claims raised, in order to identify unusual movements.
A2: The team independently executes the credit-limit control in the ERP to confirm that a shipping document is blocked when the credit limit is exceeded.
A3: The team performs a physical examination of finished goods at the Sri City plant.
A4: The team discusses with the Chief Information Security Officer whether any privileged access was granted outside the standard approval workflow.
A5: The team evaluates the trend in after-sales service spend per customer against the movement in the warranty provision.

Consider the following statements:

**Statement 1:** A2 evaluates the operating effectiveness of a control in preventing, detecting and correcting material misstatements and is therefore a test of controls.
**Statement 2:** A1 and A5 are substantive analytical procedures, being evaluations of financial information by study of plausible relationships among both financial and non-financial data.
**Statement 3:** A3, being a physical examination of an asset, is a method of obtaining evidence and is not itself a classification of audit procedure.
**Statement 4:** A4 cannot form part of any audit procedure because responses to inquiries may provide only corroborative audit evidence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 hold. A2 is a test of controls because the auditor independently executes the control; A1 and A5 are substantive analytical procedures because they evaluate financial information through plausible relationships with non-financial data such as units shipped and customer counts; and A3 uses inspection as its method while the classification of that work depends on the purpose for which it is done. Statement 4 misreads the source, since the words about corroborative audit evidence describe the character of evidence obtained by a method and do not exclude inquiry from any procedure.

questions.question:
Case study: In planning the audit of Kavach Sentinel Systems Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement team performs five activities:
A1: The team studies the relationship between units shipped, the size of the installed base and warranty claims raised, in order to identify unusual movements.
A2: The team independently executes the credit-limit control in the ERP to confirm that a shipping document is blocked when the credit limit is exceeded.
A3: The team performs a physical examination of finished goods at the Sri City plant.
A4: The team discusses with the Chief Information Security Officer whether any privileged access was granted outside the standard approval workflow.
A5: The team evaluates the trend in after-sales service spend per customer against the movement in the warranty provision.

Assertion (A): Activity A1 can be performed as a risk assessment procedure.

Reason (R): Risk assessment procedures are the audit procedures to identify the risk of material misstatement, as given in SA 315.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: A1 studies plausible relationships among financial and non-financial data to identify unusual movements, which is the analytical procedures method applied to the identification of risk. R correctly states what risk assessment procedures are, and it explains A because the very purpose it recites, identifying the risk of material misstatement, is what the unusual movements produced by A1 are being used for. The point tested is that a method from the methods table is not itself a classification of procedure, so the same analytical work can be performed under risk assessment procedures or as a substantive analytical procedure depending on the purpose.

questions.question:
Case study: In planning the audit of Kavach Sentinel Systems Limited for FY 2025-26, the engagement team performs five activities:
A1: The team studies the relationship between units shipped, the size of the installed base and warranty claims raised, in order to identify unusual movements.
A2: The team independently executes the credit-limit control in the ERP to confirm that a shipping document is blocked when the credit limit is exceeded.
A3: The team performs a physical examination of finished goods at the Sri City plant.
A4: The team discusses with the Chief Information Security Officer whether any privileged access was granted outside the standard approval workflow.
A5: The team evaluates the trend in after-sales service spend per customer against the movement in the warranty provision.

Assertion (A): Activity A5 is a substantive procedure rather than a test of controls.

Reason (R): An analytical procedure is always a substantive procedure and is never capable of being used for any other purpose.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion is correct: A5 evaluates the warranty provision through relationships between spend per customer and the movement in the provision, that is, it is designed to detect a material misstatement in a balance, which makes it a substantive analytical procedure and hence a substantive procedure. The reason is incorrect because the source places analytical procedures in the table of methods used to obtain evidence in performing the above procedures, a description wide enough to cover risk assessment work as well, as activity A1 in the same case shows. A candidate who accepts the reason will usually also misclassify A1.

questions.question:
Case study: Vayu Earthmovers Limited carries 41 separate comprehensive insurance policies for its specialised earth-moving fleet, aggregating a book value of Rs. 3.85 crore, against planning materiality of Rs. 1.60 crore. Because the population is small and each item is individually material, the auditor examines all 41 policy wordings and expiry endorsements, extracting no subset and isolating no individually chosen items. The audit senior suggests that this is in substance audit sampling spread over the entire book.

Which one of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE response to the senior's suggestion?
options: He is right, because any examination of a population of more than forty items is treated as audit sampling.
He is wrong, because examining all items is 100% examination, which is one of the three approaches to selecting items for testing and is distinct from audit sampling.
He is wrong, because the work is properly characterised as selecting specific items, the whole book being individually material.
He is right, because 100% examination and audit sampling are the same approach under different names.
He is wrong, because the work is a substantive analytical procedure rather than a selection of items for testing.
questions.explanation: The source sets out three approaches to selecting items for testing: selecting all items, that is, 100% examination, selecting specific items and audit sampling. Examining all 41 policies is 100% examination, and the two options that equate it with sampling collapse two distinct approaches into one. Option 3 mislabels the work as selecting specific items, which it is not because no subset was isolated. Option 5 moves the activity into the components of substantive procedures, which is a different row of the same framework and answers a different question.

questions.question:
Case study: Vayu Earthmovers Limited carries 41 separate comprehensive insurance policies for its specialised earth-moving fleet, aggregating a book value of Rs. 3.85 crore, against planning materiality of Rs. 1.60 crore. Because the population is small and each item is individually material, the auditor examines all 41 policy wordings and expiry endorsements, extracting no subset and isolating no individually chosen items. The audit senior suggests that this is in substance audit sampling spread over the entire book.

Consider the following statements about selecting items for testing:

**Statement 1:** The approaches available are selecting all items, that is, 100% examination, selecting specific items, and audit sampling.
**Statement 2:** On the facts described, the approach actually used is 100% examination, since all items in the population were examined.
**Statement 3:** Selecting specific items and audit sampling are the same approach expressed in different language.
**Statement 4:** Audit sampling means examining only those items exceeding planning materiality, so the work described is audit sampling.

Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 3 and 4 are the incorrect ones. Statement 3 merges two of the three approaches the source lists side by side, and statement 4 redefines audit sampling as a high-value-item filter, which is not what the taxonomy says sampling is. Statement 1 reproduces the three-way taxonomy and statement 2 applies it correctly to facts in which no subset was extracted. The candidate must resist the suggestion embedded in the case that examining a whole population is sampling with complete coverage.

questions.category: SA 500 – Integrated: Procedures, Methods and Management's Expert
questions.question:
Case study: In the audit of Nalin Sindhu Financiers Limited for FY 2025-26, the entity recognises a lease modification whose residual-value component rests on an actuarial present-value computation prepared by an actuarial firm engaged by the entity, the firm having no connection with the auditor's firm. Before the partner decides how to treat that computation, the team performs three further activities: X1, a discussion with the entity's treasury team to understand how the modified lease was negotiated; X2, a study of the relationship between the portfolio's disbursal volumes, the number of branches and interest income for the year; and X3, obtaining from the lessor a direct written response addressed to the auditor confirming the outstanding rentals.

Consider the following statements:

**Statement 1:** X3 is external confirmation, being audit evidence obtained by the auditor as a direct written response to the auditor from a third party, the confirming party.
**Statement 2:** X1 and X2 are both inquiry because each consists of obtaining information rather than examining a record.
**Statement 3:** The actuarial firm's computation is audit evidence, since audit evidence includes both financial information and other information used by the auditor in arriving at the conclusions on which the opinion is based.
**Statement 4:** The engagement partner must evaluate the competence, capability and objectivity of the actuarial firm, obtain an understanding of its work and evaluate the appropriateness of its work as audit evidence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is the error. X1 is inquiry because it seeks information of knowledgeable persons within the entity, but X2 is an analytical procedure, being an evaluation of financial information by study of plausible relationships among both financial and non-financial data, so the two activities fall in different rows of the methods table. Statement 1 is the definition of external confirmation and the directness of the lessor's reply is the decisive fact. Statement 3 follows from the inclusive definition of audit evidence, and statement 4 from the three shall requirements triggered by evidence prepared using the work of a management's expert, the actuarial firm being an expert in a field other than accounting or auditing whose work is used by the entity.

questions.question:
SA 501 'Audit Evidence – Specific Considerations for Selected Items' sets out specific considerations for obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence in respect of which of the following items?

**Statement 1:** Inventory.
**Statement 2:** Litigation and claims.
**Statement 3:** Segment information.
**Statement 4:** External confirmations of trade receivables from customers.

Which of the above are the items for which SA 501 provides specific considerations?
questions.explanation: SA 501 addresses specific considerations for inventory, litigation and claims, and segment information, so statements 1, 2 and 3 fall within its scope. External confirmations of trade receivables are dealt with under a different standard (SA 505) and are not one of SA 501's three named items, making statement 4 incorrect. The decisive fact is the source's own scope sentence, which lists exactly three areas. A candidate who treats any confirmation procedure as part of SA 501 overstates its scope.

questions.question:
Case Study: Vardhman Forgings Ltd manufactures industrial valves. Inventory (raw steel, work-in-progress and finished goods) is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The company conducted its physical inventory counting on 28 November 2024 and maintains a perpetual inventory system. In his planning note, the in-charge states that, on attending the count, the team proposes to (a) evaluate management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the count, (b) observe the counting procedures carried out by company staff, (c) inspect the warehouse inventory, and (d) perform test counts of selected items; he also notes that the team will agree the entity's final inventory record to the general ledger.

With reference to SA 501, which of the following are among the things the auditor does on attending the physical inventory counting?

**Statement 1:** Evaluate management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the physical counting.
**Statement 2:** Observe management's counting procedures.
**Statement 3:** Inspect the inventory with a view to identifying obsolete, damaged or ageing inventory.
**Statement 4:** Verify the legal ownership / title of all inventory items.

Select the correct combination.
questions.explanation: On attending the count SA 501 lists evaluating management's instructions and procedures, observing the counting, inspecting inventory, and performing test counts; inspecting for obsolete, damaged or ageing inventory is expressly part of that. Verifying legal title is not one of the four attendance activities and would import an ownership assertion SA 501 does not attach to attendance. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are therefore correct and statement 4 is not. The decisive fact is that attendance tests existence and condition, not rights.

questions.question:
Case Study: Vardhman Forgings Ltd manufactures industrial valves. Inventory (raw steel, work-in-progress and finished goods) is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The company conducted its physical inventory counting on 28 November 2024 and maintains a perpetual inventory system. In his planning note, the in-charge states that, on attending the count, the team proposes to (a) evaluate management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the count, (b) observe the counting procedures carried out by company staff, (c) inspect the warehouse inventory, and (d) perform test counts of selected items; he also notes that the team will agree the entity's final inventory record to the general ledger.

The engagement team debates the precise objective for which SA 501 requires the auditor to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding inventory when inventory is material to the financial statements. Which one of the following most accurately states that objective?
options: Ownership and valuation of the inventory
Existence and condition of the inventory
Completeness and rights in the inventory
Costing and net realisable value of the inventory
questions.explanation: SA 501 expressly frames the inventory objective as obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the existence and condition of inventory, obtained by attending the physical count if practical. Ownership, rights, valuation, costing and net realisable value are not the stated objective of this requirement, so the options mixing them are wrong. The decisive fact is the exact phrase used by the standard. Candidates frequently add valuation because inspection surfaces obsolete stock, but that is the means, not the stated objective.

questions.question:
Case Study: Vardhman Forgings Ltd manufactures industrial valves. Inventory (raw steel, work-in-progress and finished goods) is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The company conducted its physical inventory counting on 28 November 2024 and maintains a perpetual inventory system. In his planning note, the in-charge states that, on attending the count, the team proposes to (a) evaluate management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the count, (b) observe the counting procedures carried out by company staff, (c) inspect the warehouse inventory, and (d) perform test counts of selected items; he also notes that the team will agree the entity's final inventory record to the general ledger.

Because the physical count was conducted on 28 November 2024 while the financial statements are as at 31 March 2025, SA 501 additionally requires the auditor to take certain steps. Which of the following actions should the auditor take in these circumstances?

**Action 1:** Perform audit procedures to obtain evidence whether changes in inventory between the count date and the date of the financial statements are properly recorded.
**Action 2:** Consider whether the perpetual inventory records are properly adjusted.
**Action 3:** Consider the reliability of the entity's perpetual inventory records and the reasons for any significant difference between the physical count and the perpetual records.
**Action 4:** Re-perform the entire physical inventory count at 31 March 2025.

Select the correct combination.
questions.explanation: When the count is at a date other than the reporting date, SA 501 adds procedures over intervening inventory changes and three considerations: whether perpetual records are properly adjusted, their reliability, and reasons for significant differences between physical count and perpetual records. Re-performing the whole count at the year-end date is not required by the standard, so action 4 is wrong. The decisive fact is that the gap between count date and FS date drives these extra steps. Actions 1 to 3 map exactly onto the standard.

questions.question:
Case Study: Vardhman Forgings Ltd manufactures industrial valves. Inventory (raw steel, work-in-progress and finished goods) is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The company conducted its physical inventory counting on 28 November 2024 and maintains a perpetual inventory system. In his planning note, the in-charge states that, on attending the count, the team proposes to (a) evaluate management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the count, (b) observe the counting procedures carried out by company staff, (c) inspect the warehouse inventory, and (d) perform test counts of selected items; he also notes that the team will agree the entity's final inventory record to the general ledger.

What changes if one fact changes? Assume instead that the physical inventory counting had been conducted exactly on 31 March 2025, the date of the financial statements. Which requirement, present under the original facts, would no longer be specifically triggered by that single fact change?
options: Evaluation of management's instructions and procedures for recording and controlling the results of the count
Procedures to obtain evidence about whether changes in inventory between the count date and the reporting date are properly recorded, together with the perpetual-record considerations
questions.explanation: The intervening-changes procedures and the three perpetual-record considerations are triggered only when the count is held at a date other than the reporting date; if the count coincides with the FS date there is no gap to bridge. Evaluating management's instructions, observing the count and performing test counts are attendance activities that apply whatever the count date is. The decisive fact is the alignment of count date with the reporting date. This isolates precisely the one requirement that disappears.

questions.question:
Case Study: Himalayan Chemex Ltd stores a hazardous, highly reactive chemical intermediate that is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The physical inventory counting is scheduled at the company's hillside storage depot, and the engagement team plans to attend on the scheduled date. Consider each of the following independent situations: (Situation 1) On the morning of the planned count date the only road to the depot is closed by a sudden landslide, so the team cannot reach the site on the planned date. (Situation 2) The depot stores bulk containers under a pressure hazard; entering during the count would expose the auditor to a genuine risk of physical injury. (Situation 3) The team lead argues that attending is impracticable simply because the depot is a long, tiring journey from the city office.

In Situation 1 (the landslide on the planned count date), what does SA 501 require the auditor to do?
options: Make or observe some physical counts on an alternative date and perform audit procedures on intervening transactions
Perform only alternative audit procedures such as inspecting documentation of subsequent sales, without any physical count
Immediately modify the audit report for a scope limitation because attendance failed
Conclude that attendance is impracticable because of the safety of the auditor
questions.explanation: Situation 1 is inability to attend on the planned date due to unforeseen circumstances, for which SA 501 prescribes making or observing physical counts on an alternative date and performing procedures on intervening transactions. Treating it as impracticable (which is about safety/nature/location) or jumping straight to modification misclassifies the trigger. Substituting only documentary procedures without any count understates the requirement. The decisive fact is that the obstruction is temporary and unforeseen, not a genuine impracticability.

questions.question:
Case Study: Himalayan Chemex Ltd stores a hazardous, highly reactive chemical intermediate that is material to its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The physical inventory counting is scheduled at the company's hillside storage depot, and the engagement team plans to attend on the scheduled date. Consider each of the following independent situations: (Situation 1) On the morning of the planned count date the only road to the depot is closed by a sudden landslide, so the team cannot reach the site on the planned date.
